answer: An agent economy resists sybils via unique-network-path proofs. Each candidate must show a distinct routable connection - a real bridge to the network - rather than cloning one virtual identity. To qualify, the route must differ from every other node, so an attacker seeding fake agents in one cold tundra datacenter cannot share a link. Honest operators near their own orchard of servers each expose a separable route. Cost is concrete: renting distinct ISP paths or ASNs per identity, plus a stake bond forfeited if two claims collide. Mass impersonation stops paying off.
